fr:merci.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|fr|frm|merci,mercy}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|merci}}, from {{inh|fr|la|mercēs|mercēdem|t=wages, fee, price}}.

Used as an interjection of gratitude since at least the early 12th century, originally as {{m|fr||grand merci}}, for instance spelled {{m|fro||granz merciz}} in ''{{w|Li coronemenz Looïs}}''.

fr:oui.raw:
===Etymology===
{{etydate|1380}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|oil|oïl}} (1100), from {{inh|fr|la-vul|*hoc ille}} or by surface analysis a compound of Old French {{m|fro|o|pos=affirmative particle}} and {{m|fro|il||he}}. Partially cognate to {{cog|oc|òc||yes}} and {{cog|ca|oi||isn't it?}}. See the Old French term for details.

fr:au revoir.raw:
===Etymology===
{{lit|until the reseeing}}. Ultimately from {{m+|la|ad}} + {{m+|la|illum}} + {{m+|la|re-}} + {{m+|la|videō}}. Cognate with {{m+|it|arrivederci}}, {{cog|ro|la revedere}}, and {{cog|ca|a reveure}}.

Compare {{cog|es|hasta la vista}} as well as parallel and more distant cognates {{cog|bg|довиждане}}, {{cog|ru|до свида́ния}}, {{cog|uk|до побачення}}, {{cog|pl|do zobaczenia}}, and {{cog|ar|إلى اللقاء}}.

fr:sœur.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|soeur}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|suer}} (nominative), from {{inh|fr|la|soror}} (cf. also the Old French oblique form {{m|fro|seror}} from the Latin accusative {{m|la|sorōrem}}), from {{inh|fr|itc-pro|*swezōr}}, ultimately from {{inh|fr|ine-pro|*swésōr}}.

fr:femme.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|femme}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|fame,feme,fenme,femme}}, from {{inh|fr|la|femina}}; ultimately from {{inh|fr|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁m̥h₁néh₂|*dʰeh₁-m̥h₁n-éh₂|t=(the one) nursing, breastfeeding}}, derivation of the verbal root {{m|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁(y)-||to suck, suckle}}.

The Old French pronunciation was {{IPAchar|[fɛ̃mə]}}, which then became {{IPAchar|[fãmə]}} through lowering of nasal vowels, finally {{IPAchar|[famə]}} in Middle French through denasalisation before {{IPAchar|/m/|/n/}}. Other words in which ''-e-'' is pronounced {{IPAchar|/a/}} include {{m|fr|[[couenne]], [[solen

fr:homme.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|homme}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|home}}, {{m|fro|hom}}, {{m|fro|hume}}, {{m|fro|homme}}, etc, from {{inh|fr|la|homō|hominem}} (with the loss of the ''-in-'' syllable, via syncope and then assimilation of ''-mn-'' to ''-mm-''), from {{inh|fr|itc-ola|hemō}}, from {{inh|fr|itc-pro|*hemō}}, from {{inh|fr|ine-pro|*ǵʰmṓ||earthling}}. Compare {{cog|ca|home}}, {{cog|it|uomo}}, {{cog|pt|homem}}, {{cog|ro|om}}, {{cog|sc|òmine}}, {{cog|nap|ommo}}, {{cog|es|hombre}}. Also {{doublet|fr|on|nocap=1}}, derived from the nominative of Latin {{m|la|homō}}.

Further cognates in regional la

fr:oiseau.raw:
===Etymology===
{{etymon|fr|:inh|frm:oyseau}}
{{inh+|fr|frm|oyseau}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|oisel}} {{circa2|1100|short=yes}}, from {{inh|fr|la-lat|aucellus|t=little bird|g=m}}, a diminutive ultimately based on {{der|fr|la|avis|t=bird|g=f}}, from {{der|fr|itc-pro|*awis}}, from {{der|fr|ine-pro|*h₂éwis}}. Compare {{cog|nrf|ouaîsé}}, {{cog|frp|usél}}.

Compare also the French {{m|fr|oie||goose}}, derived from another diminutive of {{m|la|avis}}.

fr:canard.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|canard}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|canart}}, {{m|fro|quanart|t=duck}}, from {{m|fro|cane|t=female duck", also "boat}}, perhaps ultimately from the same {{onomatopoeic|fr|title=imitative}} root as {{m|fro|caner|t=to cackle, prattle}} {{gl|although ''caner'' is attested later than ''canart''}} or from {{inh|fr|fro|cane|t=boat, ship; waterbird}}, from {{der|fr|frk|*kanō|t=boat, floating vessel}}, from {{der|fr|gem-pro|*kanô|t=boat, vessel}}, from {{der|fr|ine-pro|*gan-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*gandʰ-|t=vessel, tub}}.

Compare {{cog|no|kane||swan-shaped vessel}}, <!-- NOT with nl:kan

fr:légume.raw:
===Etymology===
{{bor+|fr|la|legūmen}} (cf. older form {{m|fr|lesgum}}); was once {{l|en|feminine|id=noun}} and became {{l|en|masculine|id=noun}} by the 17th century. Replaced the {{cog|fro|leun|leün}}, which was inherited from the same source. Compare {{cog|it,pt|legume}}, {{cog|ca|llegum}}, {{cog|es|legumbre}}.

fr:vert.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|verd}}, {{m|frm|vert}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|vert}}, from {{inh|fr|la-lat|virdis}}, syncopated from Classical {{inh|fr|la|viridis}}. Compare {{cog|it,pt,es|verde}}. The {{m+|fro||-t}} is due to regular final devoicing. The feminine was originally also {{m|fro||vert}} and was extended with {{m|fr||-e}} only during Middle French times, thus keeping the
devoiced sound.

fr:blanc.raw:
===Etymology===
{{ety|fr|:inh|frm:blanc}}
{{inh+|fr|frm|blanc}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|blanc}}, {{m|fro|branc}}, from {{inh|fr|la-eme|blancus}}, a borrowing of {{der|fr|frk|*blank}}, from {{der|fr|gem-pro|*blankaz||bright, shining, blinding, white}}, from {{der|fr|ine-pro|*bʰleyǵ-||to shine}}.

Akin to {{cog|goh|blanch||bright, white}} ({{cog|de|blank||polished, naked}}), {{cog|non|blankr||white}} ({{cog|da|blank||bright, shiny}}), {{cog|nl|blank||white, shining}}. More at {{m|en|blink}}, {{m|en|blank}}.

fr:orange.raw:
===Etymology===
{{etymon|fr|:inh|frm:orange<id:fruit>|id=fruit}}
{{inh+|fr|frm|orange}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|orenge}}, short form of late {{m|fro|pomme d'orenge}} or ''pomme d'orange'', which was calqued after {{der|fr|roa-oit|melarancia}} ({{m|it|mela}} + {{m|it|arancia}}). The ''o'' came into the word under influence of the place name {{m|fr|Orange}}.
See {{m+|en|orange}}.

fr:gris.raw:
===Etymology===
{{der+|fr|fro|-}} or {{der|fr|pro|-}}, both from {{der|fr|frk|*grīs}}, from {{der|fr|gem-pro|*grīsaz|t=grey}}. Akin to {{cog|goh|grīs||grey}} ({{cog|de|greis}}) and {{cog|nl|grijs|t=grey}}. More at {{m|en|grizzle}}.

fr:un.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|un}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|un}}, from {{inh|fr|la|ūnum}}, accusative singular of {{m|la|ūnus||one}}, from {{inh|fr|itc-ola|oinos}}, from {{inh|fr|itc-pro|*oinos}}, from {{inh|fr|ine-pro|*h₁óynos}}.

fr:cinq.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|fr|frm|cinq}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|cinc}}, from {{inh|fr|la-vul|cīnque}}, [[dissimilation]] of Classical {{inh|fr|la|quīnque||five}}, from {{inh|fr|itc-pro|*kʷenkʷe}}, from {{inh|fr|ine-pro|*pénkʷe}}, cognate with {{cog|pt|-}} and {{cog|es|cinco}}, {{cog|it|cinque}}. {{doublet|fr|punch}}.

fr:six.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|six}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|sis}}, {{m|fro|six}}, from {{inh|fr|la|sex}}, from {{inh|fr|ine-pro|*swéḱs}}.

The numbers {{m|fr||six}} and {{m|fr|dix|t=ten}}, as well as the pronoun {{m|fr|tous|t=all}}, are remnants of the Old and Middle French pronunciation system where final ''-s'' or ''-x'' was silent before consonants, pronounced {{IPAchar-lite|/z/}} before vowels, and {{IPAchar-lite|/s/}} in [[pausa]]. The only change is that the pausal pronunciation is now invariably used when these words do not precede their referent.

fr:huit.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|huyct}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|uit}}, from {{inh|fr|la|octō}}, from {{inh|fr|ine-pro|*oḱtṓw}}.

The ''h-'' was added in Middle French to avoid confusion with {{m|fr|vit}} when the letters ''u'' and ''v'' were not distinguished; compare the same in {{m|fr|huile}}, etc. That {{m|fr||huit}} does not undergo initial liaison is in fact due to a general rule for numerals (compare {{m|fr|un}}, {{m|fr|onze}}), not to a historically aspirated onset.

fr:dix.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|fro|dis}}, from {{inh|fr|la|decem}}, from {{inh|fr|ine-pro|*déḱm̥}}. For the pronunciation compare {{m|fr|six}}.

fr:maison.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|-}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|maisun}}, {{m|fro|meson}}, inherited from {{inh|fr|la|mānsiō|mānsiōnem|t=abode, home, dwelling}}, from {{m|la|maneō|t=remain, stay}} (whence also {{m+|fr|manoir}}).

{{doublet|fr|mansion}}, a borrowing.

fr:porte.raw:
===Etymology 1===
{{inh+|fr|fro|porte}}, from {{inh|fr|la|porta}}, from the {{der|fr|ine-pro|-}} root {{m|ine-pro|*per-|t=to pass through}}. Compare {{cog|en|portal}}.

fr:boire.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|boire}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|boivre}}, {{m|fro|beivre}}, from {{inh|fr|la|bibō|bibere}}, from {{inh|fr|itc-pro|*pibō}}, from {{inh|fr|ine-pro|*píph₃eti}}.

{{col-top|2|More details on conjugation}}
The stressed past historic stems (1st singular, 3rd singular and 3rd plural) are from {{w|Vulgar Latin}} perfect stem ''*būb-'' (historic {{inh|fr|fro|bui}}), while the unstressed past historic (remaining past historic tenses), subjunctive imperfect, and past participle endings changed from ''-i-'' to ''-ū-'' (''*bibūstus'' → {{inh|fr|fro|beüs}}, ''*bibūtum'' → {{inh|fr|f

fr:aller.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|fr|frm|aller}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|aler}}, from {{inh|fr|la-eme|alāre}}, of uncertain origin. Forms beginning with ''v-'' come from {{inh|fr|la|vado}}; forms beginning with ''ir-'' come from {{inh|fr|la|eo}}.

fr:avoir.raw:
===Etymology===
{{etymon|fr|:inh|frm:avoir}}
{{inh+|fr|frm|avoir}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|avoir}}, {{m|fro|aveir}}, {{m|fro|aver}}, from {{inh|fr|la|habeō|habēre|t=have, hold, possess}}, probably from a {{der|fr|itc-pro|*habēō}} or {{m|itc-pro|*haβēō}}, possibly ultimately from {{der|fr|ine-pro|*gʰh₁bʰ-||to grab, to take}}. Influenced and reinforced by similar (yet etymologically unrelated) verbs in {{cog|gem}}; compare {{ncog|frk|*habbjan|t=to have}}, {{ncog|goh|habēn|t=to have}}, {{ncog|non|hafa|t=to have}}, {{ncog|got|𐌷𐌰𐌱𐌰𐌽|t=to have}}.

See closer cognates in regional languages in France:

fr:voir.raw:
===Etymology===
{{etymon|fr|:inh|frm:veoir<id:see>|id=see}}
{{inh+|fr|frm|veoir}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|veoir}}, {{m|fro|veir}}, from earlier {{m|fro|vedeir}}, from {{inh|fr|la|videō|vidēre}}, from {{inh|fr|itc-pro|*widēō}}, ultimately from {{der|fr|ine-pro|*weyd-}}. Unrelated to {{m|fr|voie}} and its derivatives and to {{m|fr|voirie}} or ''[[avoir]]''.

See cognates in regional languages in France : {{cog|nrf|veî}} or ''[[veir]]'', {{cog|roa-gal|vair}}, {{cog|pcd|vir}}, {{cog|roa-brg|voi}}, {{cog|frp|vêre}}, {{cog|oc|veire}}, {{m|oc|véder}}, {{m|oc|véser}}, {{cog|co|vedè}}, {{cog|ca|veure}}.

Se

fr:demain.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|fro|demain}}, from {{inh|fr|la-lat|dē māne|t=early in the morning}}, from {{inh|fr|la|dē}} + {{m|la|māne}}, from {{der|fr|ine-pro|*meh₂-|t=to mature, ripen}}.

fr:ici.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{der|fr|fro|ci||here}}, from {{der|fr|la-lat|ecce hīc}}, with {{IPAchar|/i-/}} added by analogy with {{der|fr|fro|iluec||there, in that place}}, from {{der|fr|la|illoc}}.

fr:facile.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|fr|frm|facile}} (15th c.), a borrowing from {{der|fr|la|facilis|t=easy}}, likely under influence of {{der|fr|it|facile}}.<!--15th-c. French was heavily influenced by Italian and cf. "faciliter", for which Trésor says this expressly-->

fr:heure.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|fr|frm|heure}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|houre}}, from {{inh|fr|la|hōra||hour}}, from {{der|fr|grc|ὥρα||time, season, year}}, from {{der|fr|ine-pro|*yóh₁r̥||year, season}}.

fr:semaine.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|sepmaine}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|semaine}}, from {{inh|fr|la-lat|septimāna||week}}, from the {{inh|fr|la|septimānus||related to the seventh element of a series|pos=adjective}}, derived from {{m|la|septimus||seventh}}.

fr:année.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|fro|anee}}. {{surf|fr|an|-ée<id:measure>}}; {{m|fr|an||year}} from {{der|fr|la|annus||year}}. Perhaps alternatively from a {{inh|fr|la-vul|*annāta}}, from {{inh|fr|la|annō|annāre}}; compare [[Italian]] {{m|it|annata|}}.

fr:toujours.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{uder|fr|frm|tousjours}}, from {{uder|fr|fro|toz jorz}}, {{m|fro|tuzjurz||without ceasing|lit=all days}}. {{surf|fr|tous|jours}} (compare {{cog|nl|altijd||always}}, {{cog|da|altid||always}}). Replaced {{m+|fro|sempres||always}}, from {{m+|la|semper}}. Cognate with {{cog|ca,oc|totjorn}}.

fr:souvent.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|fro|suvent}}, {{m|fro|sovent}}, from {{inh|fr|la|subinde}}, morphologically {{affix|la|sub|inde|nocat=1}}. The original meaning of ''subinde'' was “immediately after”, which then evolved to “repeatedly” and then to “often”.<ref>{{cite-book|fr|last=Dauzat|first=Albert|coauthors=Jean Dubois, Henri Mitterand|title=Nouveau dictionnaire étymologique|year=1964|publisher=Librairie Larousse|location=Paris}}</ref>

fr:jamais.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|fro|ja mais|t=any more|pos=only in reference to the future}}, the two components deriving from {{der|fr|la|iam}} and {{m|la|magis}}. Compare {{cog|es|jamás}}, {{cog|it|giammai}}, {{cog|oc|jamai}} and {{cog|pt|jamais}}.

fr:vent.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|vent}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|vent}}, from {{inh|fr|la|ventus}}, from {{inh|fr|itc-pro|*wentos}}, ultimately from {{inh|fr|ine-pro|*h₂wéh₁n̥ts}} < {{m|ine-pro|*h₂weh₁-|t=to blow}}.

fr:brouillard.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{af|fr|brouiller|-ard}}, restructuring of an older {{m|fro|brouillas}}, derived from the same verb.

fr:argent.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|argent|g=m}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|argent|g=m}}, from {{der|fr|la|argentum|g=n}}, according to the TLFi etymological dictionary, a borrowing).

fr:cher.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|cher}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|cher}}, {{m|fro|chier}}, from {{inh|fr|la|cārus|cārum|t=dear, valuable}}, from {{inh|fr|itc-pro|*kāros}}, from {{inh|fr|ine-pro||*kéh₂ros}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*keh₂-|gloss=to desire, to wish}}.

fr:caisse.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|caisse}}, borrowed from {{der|fr|oc|caissa}}, from {{der|fr|la|capsa}}. Compare the etymological doublets {{doublet|fr|châsse|casse|notext=1}}.

fr:triste.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|fro|triste}}, borrowed from {{der|fr|la|trīstis}}. Old French originally had {{m|fro|trist}}, inherited from Vulgar Latin {{m|la-vul|trīstus}}, a variant of the same word.

fr:malade.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|malade}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|malade}}, from {{inh|fr|la|male habitus||ill-kept, not in good condition}}.

fr:travail.raw:
===Etymology===
{{ety|fr|:inh|frm:travail<t:suffering, pain>}}
{{inh+|fr|frm|travail|t=suffering, pain}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|travail|t=suffering, pain}}, deverbal of {{m|fro|travailler}}, from {{der|fr|la-vul|*tripāliāre}}, from {{der|fr|la-lat|tripālium|t=torture device made of three stakes}}.

The plural derives from Old French {{m|fro|travauz}}, early {{m|fro|travailz}}, with vocalization of the lateral before a consonant (/tʁavo/ < /tɾaˈvau̯s/ < /tɾaˈvaʎts/).

fr:se lever.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|lever}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|lever}}, from {{inh|fr|la|levō|levāre|t=to lift; to lighten, relieve}}, from {{m|la|levis|t=light, not heavy}}.

fr:tâche.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|fro|tasche}}, from {{inh|fr|la-eme|tasca}}, variant of {{m|la|taxa}}, from {{der|fr|la|taxō||to handle, appraise}}, from {{m|la|tangō||to touch}}, from {{der|fr|ine-pro|*teh₂g-}}, cognate with {{cog|grc|τάσσω||to organise, arrange}}.

fr:salaire.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|fro|salaire}}, from {{der|fr|la|salārium}}, probably a semi-learned borrowing. Cf. also the inherited Old French {{m|fro|salier}}, {{m|fro|saler}} (and modern {{m|fr|salière}}).

fr:valise.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|valise}}, from {{der|fr|la-med|valesia}}, {{m|la|valixia}}, from {{der|fr|la-lat|valisia}}, possibly from {{der|fr|cel-gau|*valisia||leather bag}}, from {{der|fr|cel-pro|*val-||to enclose, surround}}, from {{der|fr|ine-pro|*welH-}}.<ref>{{R:American_Heritage_Dictionary}}</ref> Or, possibly from {{bor|fr|ar|وَلِيهَة||large bag}}.<ref>{{R:es:Roberts:2014}}</ref>

Maybe a borrowing through {{bor|fr|it|valigia}}, even though this is dubious. Compare {{cog|es|valija}}.<ref>http://nq.oxfordjournals.org/cgi/issue_pdf/frontmatter_pdf/s9-X/247.pdf</ref>

fr:gauche.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{m|fr|gauchir|t=to bend, dodge, warp}}, a conflation of {{der|fr|fro|gauchier|t=to tread}} (from {{der|fr|frk|*walkijan}}, {{m|frk|*walkan}}, cognate with {{cog|en|walk}}) + {{der|fr|fro|guenchir|t=to deviate}} (from {{der|fr|frk|*wankijan|*wenkijan|t=to sway, falter}}). ''Gauche'' replaced the original Latin-derived word for "left", {{m|fr|senestre}}, in the sixteenth century. Compare {{cog|wa|gåtche}}.

fr:chambre.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|fro|chambre}}, {{m|fro|cambre}}, from {{inh|fr|la|cambra}}, Medieval spelling of {{inh|fr|la|camera||[[room]]}}, from {{der|fr|grc|καμάρα||[[something]] with an [[arch]]ed [[cover]]: a [[covered]] [[wagon]], a [[covered]] [[boat]], a [[vaulted]] [[chamber]]}}. {{doublet|fr|caméra}}, a borrowing.

fr:cuisine.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|fro|cuisine||kitchen; cooking, cooked food}}, from {{inh|fr|la-lat|cocīna}}, from earlier {{m|la|coquīna||kitchen}}. {{etydate|12th century}}.<ref>{{R:Etymonline|pos=n}}</ref> Cognate with {{cog|en|kitchen}}.

fr:salon.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|-}}, from {{der|fr|it|salone||large hall}}, augmented form of {{m|it|sala||hall}}, from {{der|fr|lng|sala||room, house, entrance hall}}, from {{der|fr|gem-pro|*salą||dwelling, house, hall}}, from {{der|fr|ine-pro|*sel-||human settlement, village, dwelling}}. Cognate with {{cog|goh|sal||room, house, entrance hall}}, {{cog|ang|sæl||room, hall, castle}}, {{cog|cu|село||courtyard, village}}, {{cog|lt|sala||island}}.

fr:jardin.raw:
===Etymology===
{{ety|fr|:inh|frm:jardin<ety:inh<fro:gardin>>}}
From {{der|fr|frm|jardin}}, from {{der|fr|fro|jardin}}, from {{der|fr|la-med|jardinus||garden}}, from Old {{der|fr|frk|*gardin}}, oblique case of {{m|frk|*gardō||enclosure, yard}} (compare also {{cog|fro|jart||garden}}), from {{der|fr|gem-pro|*gardô||enclosure, garden, house}}, from {{der|fr|ine-pro|*gʰordʰos||hedge, enclosure}}, from {{der|fr|ine-pro|*gʰerdʰ-||court, yard}}.

Cognate with {{cog|goh|gart}}, {{m|goh|garto||garden, enclosure, yard}}, {{cog|ang|ġeard||garden, yard, fence, enclosure}}. Cognate with English ''[[garden]

fr:apprendre.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|apprendre}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|aprendre}}, {{m|fro|aprandre}}, inherited from {{inh|fr|la|apprendere}}, contracted form of {{m|la|apprehendō|apprehendere}}. {{doublet|fr|appréhender}}, which was borrowed.

fr:aider.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|ayder}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|aidier}}, from {{inh|fr|la|adiūtō|adiutāre|to help, assist}}. Cognate with {{cog|ca|aidar}}, {{cog|es|ayudar}}, {{cog|ro|ajuta}}, {{cog|it|aiutare}}, {{cog|pt,ca|ajudar}}.

fr:pouvoir.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|povoir}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|povoir}}, {{m|fro|pooir}}, from earlier Old French {{m|fro|poeir}}, {{m|fro|podeir}}, from {{inh|fr|la-vul|posso|potēre}}, regularization of {{inh|fr|la|possum|posse}}. The /-v-/ was eventually added, after the loss of the intervocalic dental, to break [[hiatus]]. The archaic 1SG present indicative {{m|fr|puis}} is from a {{inh|fr|la-vul||*posseō}} (rather than {{m|la-vul|possō}}), for which cf. {{cog|roa-oca|puix}}.

{{col-top|2|cog}}
See also {{cog|roa-ang|pouvoér}}, {{cog|an|poder}}, {{cog|rup|pot}}, {{m|rup|puteari}}, {{cog|ast|pode

fr:penser.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|penser}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|penser}}, from {{inh|fr|la|penso|pēnsāre}}, whence also the doublet {{doublet|fr|peser|notext=1}}, as well as {{m|fr|panser}}, originally an alternative spelling which acquired a special sense.

fr:assez.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|assez}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|asez}}, from {{inh|fr|la-lat|ad satis}}, from {{inh|fr|la|ad}} + {{m|la|satis}}. Cognate with {{cog|frp|asséds}}, {{cog|oc|assatz}}, {{cog|it|assai}}, {{cog|pt|assaz}}, and {{cog|es|asaz}}. {{doublet|fr|assai}}.

fr:trop.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|trop}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|trop||unreasonably excessive}}, from {{der|fr|frk|*þorp||a cluster, agglomeration", ''also'' "collection of houses, village}}, from {{der|fr|gem-pro|*þurpą||village}}, from {{der|fr|ine-pro|*trab-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*treb-||dwelling, room}} which are cognate with {{cog|osx|thorp||village}}, {{cog|goh|dorf||village}}, {{cog|ang|þorp||village}}. Cognate with {{cog|it|troppo}}, and {{cog|pms|tròp}}/{{m|pms|trop}}. More at {{cog|en|thorp}}, {{cog|en|troop}}.

fr:encore.raw:
===Etymology===
Probably from {{inh|fr|fro|ancor}}, from  {{der|fr|la-lat|[[in]] [[hanc]] [[hōram]]||until this hour}}. Compare {{cog|ca|-}} and {{cog|oc|encara}}, {{cog|it|ancora}}. {{semantic loan|fr|de|noch|pos=adverb|senseid=again (following a question)}}.

fr:vite.raw:
===Etymology===
{{ety|fr|:inh|fro:viste}}
From {{der|fr|fro|viste}}, of disputed origin:.

* According to Littré, from {{der|fr|it|visto||seen}}, from {{der|fr|la-vul|*visitus}}, from {{der|fr|la|vidēre}}. The adverb corresponds with {{m|fr|à vue||rapidly, without notice}}; compare {{cog|it|avvisto||noticed, adroit}}.<ref>http://artflx.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/dicos/pubdico1look.pl?strippedhw=vite&dicoid=LITTRE1872</ref>
* Derived from an {{onomatopoeic|fr|title=onomatopoeia}} expressing rapid movement.<ref>{{R:fr:TLFi}}</ref>
* From {{der|fr|la|vegetus||lively, animated}}.

fr:seulement.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|fr|frm|seullement}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|solement}}, from {{inh|fr|la-eme|sōlā mente}}. Synchronically derivable from {{af|fr|seul|-ment<id:adverbial>|alt1=seule}}.

fr:citoyen.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|citoyen}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|citoien}}, {{m|fro|citeien}}, from earlier {{m|fro|citeain}}, equivalent to {{m|fr|cité}} + {{m|fr|-ain}} (later confused with or influenced by the suffix {{m|fr|-ien}}). {{doublet|fr|citadin}}, a borrowing from Italian.

fr:entreprise.raw:
===Etymology===
{{ety|fr|entreprendre}}
Feminine past participle of {{m|fr|entreprendre||[[undertake]]}}.
Compare {{cog|it|impresa}} for a similar construction.

fr:carrière.raw:
===Etymology 1===
{{inh+|fr|frm|carriere}}. Borrowed from {{bor|fr|pro|carreira}} or {{bor|fr|it|carriera}}, itself from Old Occitan, from {{der|fr|la-lat||(via)}} {{m|la|carrāria}}, from {{der|fr|la|carrus}}. Compare the inherited doublet {{doublet|fr|charrière|notext=1}}.

fr:formation.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|fro|formacion}}, borrowed from {{bor|fr|la|fōrmātiō|fōrmātiōnem}}. Cf. also the archaic {{m|fr|formaison}}.

fr:médecin.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|medecin}}, a back-formation from {{der|fr|fro|medeciner|t=to treat medically}}. Replaced {{cog|fro|mire}}, {{m|fro|mege}}, {{m|fro|meide}}, {{m|fro|meie}}{{,}} etc. inherited from {{cog|la|medicus}}.

fr:symptôme.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{uder|fr|frm|-}} ({{m|frm|sinthome}}, Bernard de Gordon). Borrowed from {{bor|fr|la|symptōma}}, itself a borrowing from {{der|fr|grc|σύμπτωμα}}.

fr:guérir.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|guérir}}, {{m|frm|guerir}}, {{m|frm|garir}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|garir}}, {{m|fro|guarir|t=to guarantee, protect, give health to}}, from {{der|fr|frk|*warjan|t=to defend, protect}}, from {{der|fr|gem-pro|*warjaną|t=to defend, guard}}, from {{der|fr|ine-pro|*wer-|t=to cover, defend, guard, heed}}.
Cognate with {{cog|oc|garir}}, {{cog|ca,es|guarir}}, {{cog|it|guarire}}, {{cog|goh|werien|t=to defend, protect}} and {{cog|ang|werian|t=to guard, keep, defend}}.

fr:résultat.raw:
===Etymology===
{{etymon|fr|:lbor|la-med:resultātum}}
{{lbor|fr|la-med|resultātum}}, the substantivized neuter singular of {{m|la|resultātus|pos=perfect passive participle of {{m|la|resultō}}}}.

{{surf|fr|résulter|-at<id:-atum>}}.

fr:raison.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|fro|reson}}, {{m|fro|raison}}, inherited from {{inh|fr|la|ratio|ratiōnem}}. Compare the borrowed doublet {{doublet|fr|ration|notext=1}}.

fr:choix.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|choix}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|chois}}, deverbal from {{m|fro|choisir}}, {{m|fro|coisir|t=to differentiate, see distinctly}}, from {{der|fr|frk|*keusan}} (see contemporary Dutch {{m|nl|kiezen}}), ultimately from {{der|fr|gem-pro|*keusaną|t=to choose}}, from {{der|fr|ine-pro|*ǵews-|t=to choose}}. 

Akin to {{cog|goh|kiosan|t=to choose}} (whence {{cog|de|kiesen|t=to choose}}), {{cog|ang|ċēosan|t=to choose}}, {{cog|non|kjósa|t=to choose}}. More at {{cog|en|choose}}.

fr:but.raw:
===Etymology 1===
From {{der|fr|frm|but||mark, goal}}, from {{der|fr|fro|but||aim, goal, end, target}}, from {{der|fr|fro|butte||mound, knoll, target}}, from {{der|fr|frk|*but||stump, log}}, or from {{der|fr|non|bútr||log, stump, butt}}; both from {{der|fr|gem-pro|*buttaz||end, piece}}.

Cognate with {{cog|ang|butt||tree stump}}; see {{m|en|butt}}. The semantic development from "mound" to "target" is likely from [[martial]] training practice. The final {{IPAchar|/t/}} is from the old pausal and liaison pronunciation; its (partial) restoration as the basic form may have been reinforced by relat

fr:essayer.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|essayer}}, {{m|frm|essaier}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|essaiier}}, {{m|fro|essayer}}, {{m|fro|essaier}}, from {{m|fro|essay}}, {{m|fro|essai||attempt; assay; experiment}} + {{m|fro|-er||infinitive-forming suffix}}, from {{der|fr|la-lat|exagium||weight; weighing, testing on the balance}}, from {{der|fr|la|exigo|exigere}} + {{m|la|-ium}}, from {{m|la|ex-}} + {{m|la|ago|agere}}, from {{der|fr|itc-pro|*agō}}, from {{der|fr|ine-pro|*h₂éǵeti}}.

fr:choisir.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|choisir}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|choisir}}, {{m|fro|coisir||to differentiate, see distinctly}}, from {{der|fr|frk|*kauʀijan||to choose}} or {{der|fr|got|𐌺𐌰𐌿𐍃𐌾𐌰𐌽}}, both from {{der|fr|gem-pro|*kauzijaną}}, from {{der|fr|gem-pro|*keusaną||to choose, taste}}, from {{der|fr|ine-pro|*ǵews-||to choose, taste}}. 

Cognate with {{cog|frp|chouêsir||to choose}}, {{cog|gl|cousir||to discern}}, Germanic cognates include {{cog|ofs|kēra||to elect}}. Related also to {{cog|got|𐌺𐌹𐌿𐍃𐌰𐌽||to choose, examine}}, {{cog|goh|kiosan||to choose}}, {{cog|ang|ċēosan||to choose}}, {{c

fr:améliorer.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|fro|ameillorer}}, from a prefixed version of {{inh|fr|la-lat|melioro|meliōrāre}}, a verb based on {{der|fr|la|melior|meliārī|better}}. The modern French form was modified under Latin influence, hence the otherwise-unexpected {{IPAchar|/lj/}} (instead of {{IPAchar|/j/}} < {{IPAchar|/ʎ/}}).

fr:développer.raw:
===Etymology===
{{ety|fr|:inh|frm:desveloper<ety:inh<fro:desveloper<ety:af<fro:des-><fro:veloper<ety:der<la-vul:*vlopp-<ety:der<gem-pro:*wrappan-<ety:der<ine-pro:*werb-<postype:root>>>>>>>>>}}
{{inh+|fr|frm|desveloper}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|desveloper}}, from {{af|fro|des-|veloper|alt2=voloper, veloper, vloper|t2=to wrap, to wrap up|nocat=1}}, from {{der|fr|la-vul|-}} base {{m|la|*vlopp-}}, {{m|la|*wlopp-||to wrap}}, from {{der|fr|gem-pro|*wrappan-}}, {{m|gem-pro|*wlappan-||to wrap, roll up, turn, wind}}, from {{der|fr|ine-pro|*werb-||to turn, bend}} [http://www.wordnik.com/words/envelop].

Akin

fr:proposer.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|fro|proposer}}, borrowed from {{der|fr|la|prōpōnō|prōpōnere}}, altered based on French {{m|fr|poser}}.

fr:considérer.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|consyderer}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|considerer}}, borrowed from {{der|fr|la|cōnsīderō|cōnsīderāre|t=to examine, look at, inspect; to consider; to investigate}}.

fr:donc.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|fro|dunc}}, from {{inh|fr|la-vul|dunc}}, from a crossing of {{der|fr|la|tunc}} with {{m|la|dum}}. Compare {{cog|it|dunque}}, {{cog|oc|donc}} and {{cog|ca|doncs}}.

fr:malgré.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|maugré}}, {{m|frm|maulgré|lit=bad will}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|malgré}}, from {{m|fro|mal}} + {{m|fro|gré}}. Cognate with {{cog|it|malgrado}} and {{cog|ca|malgrat}}.

fr:environ.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|fro|environ|t=around}}, from {{af|fro|en|t1=in|viron|t2=a turn|nocat=1}}, from {{m|fro|virer||to turn, veer}}, whence also French {{m|fr|virer}}.

fr:quotidien.raw:
===Etymology===
{{lbor|fr|la|quotīdiānus}}, late spelling of Classical {{m|la|cottīdiānus}}, from {{m|la|cottīdiē||daily}}; cognate with {{cog|en|quotidian}}.

fr:avenir.raw:
===Etymology===
From the expression {{m|fr|temps}} {{m|fr|à}} {{m|fr|venir}} ("time (that is) to come"). Cf. also Old French {{m|fro|avenir}}.

fr:tradition.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|tradition}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|-}}, borrowed from {{bor|fr|la|trāditiō|trāditiōnem}}, from the verb {{m|la|trādere||}}. Compare {{m|fr|trahison}}.

fr:ressource.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{der|fr|la|resurgere|t=to rise again, resurface}}, itself from {{af|la|re-|t1=again|surgere|t2=to rise|nocat=1}}, from {{af|la|sub-|t1=under|regere|t2=to direct|nocat=1}}.

fr:hypothèse.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|hypothese}}, a {{lbor|fr|la-lat|hypothesis|nocap=1}}, itself borrowed from {{der|fr|grc|ὑπόθεσις|t=base, basis of an argument, supposition|lit=a placing under}}.

fr:constater.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{m|fr|constat}}, borrowed from {{der|fr|la|cōnstat}}, the third-person singular present active indicative of {{m|la|cōnstō}}. Compare also {{m|fr|coûter}}.

fr:considérable.raw:
===Etymology===
From the verbe [[considérer]] with the suffix {{l|fr|-able}}.

fr:au fur et à mesure.raw:
===Etymology===
{{lit|in proportion and measure}}. The noun {{m|fr|fur||rate, proportion}} is obsolete outside this expression.

fr:toutefois.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|toutesfoys}}, from the plurals {{m|fr|toutes}} and {{m|fr|fois}}. In Old French, the adverb was {{m|fro|totesvoies}} (from {{m|fr|voie||way}}), closer to Italian {{m|it|tuttavia}} and Portuguese {{m|pt|todavia}}.

fr:voire.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|la|vēra}}, neuter plural of {{m|la|vērus||true}}. Related to {{m|fr|vrai|t=true}}, from {{m+|la|vērāx}}.

fr:convaincre.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|fro|}}, borrowed from {{bor|fr|la|convincō|convincere}}, and adapted to the form of {{m|fr|vaincre}}.

fr:croissance.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{af|fr|croître|alt1=croiss-|-ance}}, corresponding to the rare {{cog|la|-}} form {{m|la|crēscentia}}.

de:hallo.raw:
===Etymology===
Originally used as a call to the ferryman on the other side of the bank; related to {{der|de|goh|holā}}, emphatic imperative of {{m|goh|holōn||to fetch, used especially in hailing a ferryman}}, from {{der|de|gmw-pro|*holōn|t=to fetch}}.  Also see {{cog|fr|holà||hey! stop!}}.

de:nein.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|nein}}, from a contraction of {{der|de|goh|ni}} {{m|goh|ein}}. Compare {{cog|ang|nān}}, from {{m|ang|ne}} {{m|ang|ān}} (Modern {{cog|en|none}}, further contracted to {{m|en|no}}).

de:tschüss.raw:
===Etymology===
{{bor+|de|nds-de|tschüß}} from earlier {{m|nds|adjüs}}, from {{der|de|nl|adjuus}}, from {{der|de|es|adiós}} or {{der|de|fr|adieu}}.<ref>{{R:de:Kluge|ed=24}}</ref> (Compare the origin of {{m|de|moin}}.)

de:Mutter.raw:
===Etymology 1===
From {{inh|de|gmh|muoter}}, from {{inh|de|goh|muoter}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*mōder}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*mōdēr}}, from {{inh|de|ine-pro|*méh₂tēr}}. Compare {{cog|nl|moeder}}, {{cog|en|mother}}, {{cog|da|moder}}, {{cog|sv|moder}}.

de:Freund.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|de|gmh|vriunt}}, from {{inh|de|goh|friunt}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*friund}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*frijōndz||lit., the [[loving]] one; [[lover]], [[loved one]], friend}}, from a derivative of {{der|de|ine-pro|*preyH-}}.

Cognate with {{cog|nl|vriend}}, {{cog|nds-de|Fründ}}, {{cog|lb|Frënd}}, {{cog|fy|freon}}, {{cog|en|friend}}, {{cog|da|frænde||relative}}, {{cog|fo|frændi||friend, relative}}, {{cog|is|frændi||relative}}, {{cog|nb|frende||relative}}, {{cog|nn|frende||relative}}, {{cog|sv|frände||relative}}, {{cog|cy|ffrind||friend}}, {{cog|yi|פֿרײַנד||friend}}, {{cog|go

de:Frau.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|vrouwe}}, from {{inh|de|goh|frouwa|t=mistress}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*frauwjā}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*frawjǭ}}, a feminine form of {{m|gem-pro|*frawjô||lord}}, giving {{cog|ang|frēa|t=lord, king; God, Christ; husband}}, {{m|ang|frēo|t=woman}}, from {{der|de|ine-pro|*proHwo-}}, a derivation from {{m|ine-pro|*per-|t=to go forward}}. 

Cognate with {{cog|osx|frūa}} (hence {{cog|gml|vrouwe}}, Modern {{cog|nds|frug}}), {{cog|non|freyja}} and {{m|non|frú}} (hence {{cog|is|frú}} and {{cog|no|frue}}). Further cognates include {{cog|de|Fron|t=corvée, soccage}} and

de:Großvater.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{compound|de|groß|Vater}}. Cognate to {{cog|nl|grootvader}}, {{cog|nds-de|Grautvader}} {{q|Paderbornisch}}. Displaced {{ncog|gmh|eltervater}}, {{m|gmh|altervater|t=grandfather}}. Compare {{cog|en|grandfather}}, which displaced {{ncog|en|eldfather}}, {{m|en|elderfather}} in a similar manner.

de:Vogel.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|vogel}}, {{m|gmh|vagel}}, from {{inh|de|goh|fogal}}, {{m|goh|fugal}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*fugl}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*fuglaz}}; possibly related to {{m|gem-pro|*fleuganą|t=to fly}} through dissimilation from earlier {{m|gem-pro|*fluglaz}}. Cognates include {{cog|nds|Vagel}}, {{cog|nl|vogel}}, {{cog|en|fowl}}, {{cog|da|fugl}}, {{cog|sv|fågel}}, {{cog|got|𐍆𐌿𐌲𐌻𐍃||}}.

de:Pferd.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|phert}}, {{m|gmh|phærît}}, {{m|gmh|pherit}}, {{m|gmh|pferift||riding horse}}, from {{inh|de|goh|pherit}}, {{m|goh|pfarifrit}}, {{m|goh|parafred}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*parafred}}, from {{der|de|la-lat|paraverēdus}} (originally “substitute post horse”). Largely displaced the native word {{m|de|Ross}}. Compare {{cog|nl|paard}} and {{cog|en|palfrey}}.

de:Hase.raw:
===Etymology 1===
From {{inh|de|gmh|hase|has(e)}}, from {{inh|de|goh|haso}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*hasō}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*hesô}}, from an {{der|de|ine|-}} root originally meaning [[grey]].

de:Wasser.raw:
===Etymology===
{{etymon|de|id=water|:inh|gmh:waȥȥer<id:water>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|waȥȥer}}, from {{inh|de|goh|waȥȥar}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*watar}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*watōr}}, from {{inh|de|ine-pro|*wédōr}}, collective of {{m|ine-pro|*wódr̥}}. 

Compare {{cog|nds|Water}}, {{cog|nl|water}}, {{cog|en|water}}, {{cog|da|vand}}.

de:Brot.raw:
===Etymology===
{{etymon|de|:inh|gmh:brōt<id:bread>|id=bread}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|brōt}}, from {{inh|de|goh|brōt}} (attested since the 8th century), from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*braud}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*braudą}}, from {{der|de|ine-pro|*bʰrew-||to seethe, to boil}}. 

Originally, the meaning of ''Brot'' was ''"what has been fermented, leaven"'' and may be a nominal derivative from {{cog|gem-pro|*brewwaną||to brew}} (whence German {{m|de|brauen}}). It replaced the older {{m|de|Laib||loaf}} which was the more common term in Old High German (compare the use of {{m|ang|hlāf}} and {{m|ang|brēad}} in

de:Kaffee.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{bor|de|fr|café}}, from {{der|de|it|caffè}}, from {{der|de|ota|قهوه|tr=kahve}}, from {{der|de|ar|قَهْوة}}. {{etydate|17th century}}. The variants with ''-o-'', which fell into disuse around 1800, are from {{cog|nl|koffie}} and {{m+|en|coffee}}. {{doublet|de|Café}}.

de:Gemüse.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|gemüese}}, a derivative of {{der|de|goh|muos||food, victuals, porridge}}, from {{der|de|gem-pro|*mōsą||porridge, food}}, from {{der|de|ine-pro|*meh₂d-|id=wet|t=wet, fat, dripping}}. {{surf|de|ge-|Mus|-e}}. Cognate to {{cog|bar|Gmias}}, {{cog|pdc|Gemies}}, {{cog|lb|Geméis}}, and possibly {{cog|en|mush}}.

de:Ei.raw:
===Etymology===
{{ety|de|:inh|gmh:ei|tree=1}}
{{inh+|de|gmh|ei}} and {{inh|de|goh|ei}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*aij}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*ajją}}, from {{inh|de|ine-pro|*h₂ōwyóm}}.

Cognate with {{cog|yi|איי}}, {{cog|nl|ei}}, {{cog|fy|aai}}, {{cog|en|ey}} and {{m|en|egg}}, {{cog|da|æg}}.

de:rot.raw:
===Etymology===
{{ety|de|:inh|gmh:rōt<t:red, red-haired><ety:inh<goh:rōt<t:red, scarlet, purple-red, brown-red, yellow-red>>>}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|rōt||red, red-haired}}, from {{inh|de|goh|rōt||red, scarlet, purple-red, brown-red, yellow-red}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*raud}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*raudaz}}, from {{inh|de|ine-pro|*h₁rowdʰós}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*h₁rewdʰ-}}. 

Compare {{cog|nds|root}}, {{m|nds|rod}}, {{m|nds|rot}}, {{cog|nl|rood}}, {{cog|en|red}}, {{cog|fy|read}}, {{cog|da|rød}}.

de:schwarz.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|swarz}}, from {{inh|de|goh|swarz}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*swart}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*swartaz}}, from {{der|de|ine-pro|*swerd-||dirty, dark, black}}.

Compare {{cog|nl|zwart}}, {{cog|en|swart}} and {{m|en|swarthy}}, {{cog|fy|swart}}, {{cog|da|sort}}, {{cog|yi|שוואַרץ}}.

de:gelb.raw:
===Etymology===
{{root|de|ine-pro|*ǵʰelh₃-}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|gel}} (inflected {{m|gmh|gelwe}}), from {{inh|de|goh|gelo}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*gelu}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*gelwaz}}. 

The form {{m|de||gelb}} is derived from the Middle High German inflected stem (as in {{m|de|herb}}), while the variant {{m|de|gehl}} is from the uninflected stem and from dialects that reduce ''-lw-'' to ''-l-'' in all positions (as in {{m|de|fahl}}, {{m|de|kahl}}). It survives in set phrases. Cognate with {{cog|nl|geel}}, {{cog|nds|geel}}, {{cog|en|yellow}}.

de:eins.raw:
===Etymology 1===
Contraction of {{m|de|eines|pos=nominative/accusative neuter of {{m|de|ein}}}}, from {{inh|de|gmh|einez}}, ultimately from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*ainatō}}, form of {{m|gem-pro|*ainaz||one}}.

de:zwei.raw:
===Etymology===
{{etymon|de|:inh|gmh:zwene}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|zwei}}, from {{inh|de|goh|zwei}} (neuter of {{m|goh|zwēne}}).

Compare {{cog|nl|twee}}, {{cog|en|two}}, {{m|en|twain}}. In Old High German, and still today in some dialects, distinct forms are used for the three grammatical genders. ''Zwei'' was originally the neuter form, now used for all genders. The Old High German masculine {{m|goh|zwēne}} is found back in early modern {{m+|de|zween}}; the feminine {{m|goh|zwō}} lives on in the variant {{m|de|zwo}} (but now without any gender distinction).

de:sieben.raw:
===Etymology 1===
From {{inh|de|gmh|siben}}, from {{inh|de|goh|sibun}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*sebun}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*sebun}}, from earlier {{inh|de|gem-pro|*sebunt}}, from {{inh|de|ine-pro|*septḿ̥}}.

Compare {{cog|nl|zeven}}, {{cog|en|seven}}.

de:acht.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|ahte}}, from {{inh|de|goh|ahto}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*ahtō}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*ahtōu}}, from {{inh|de|ine-pro|*oḱtṓw}}.

Compare {{cog|nl|acht}}, {{cog|en|eight}}, {{cog|da|otte}}, {{cog|sv|åtta}}, {{cog|el|οκτώ}}, {{cog|la|octō}}.

de:zehn.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|zehen}}, from {{inh|de|goh|zehan}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|-}} and {{inh|de|gem-pro|*tehun|t=ten}}, from {{inh|de|ine-pro|*déḱm̥|t=ten}}. Compare {{cog|nl|tien}}, {{cog|nds|teihn}}, {{cog|en|ten}}, {{cog|got|𐍄𐌰𐌹𐌷𐌿𐌽}}.

de:Haus.raw:
===Etymology===
{{ety|de|:inh|gmh:hūs|tree=1}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|hūs}}, from {{inh|de|goh|hūs}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*hūs}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*hūsą}}.

Cognate with {{cog|ofs|hūs}}, {{cog|nds|[[Hus]], [[Huus]]}}, {{cog|nl|huis}}, {{cog|is|hús}}, {{cog|fo|hús}}, {{cog|da|hus}}, {{cog|no|hus}}, {{cog|sv|hus}}, {{cog|en|house}}. {{doublet|de|House}}.

de:Bett.raw:
===Etymology===
{{dercat|de|ine-pro}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|bet}}, {{m|gmh|bette}}, from {{inh|de|goh|betti}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*badi}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*badją}} (“plot, grave, resting-place, bed”).

Cognate with {{cog|nds|Bedd}}, {{cog|nl|bed}}, {{cog|fy|bêd}}, {{cog|en|bed}}, {{cog|sv|bädd}}, {{cog|is|beður}}. {{doublet|de|Beet}}.

de:essen.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|ëȥȥen}}, from {{inh|de|goh|ëȥȥan}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*etan}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*etaną}}, from {{der|de|ine-pro|*h₁ed-}}.

Cognate with {{cog|nds|eten}}, {{cog|gsw|ässe}}, {{cog|nl|eten}}, {{cog|en|eat}}, {{cog|da|æde}}, {{cog|no|ete}}, {{cog|sv|äta}}, {{cog|yi|עסן}} and {{cog|got|𐌹𐍄𐌰𐌽}}. Non-Germanic cognates include {{cog|la|edō}}, {{cog|ru|есть}}, {{cog|gd|ith}}.

de:trinken.raw:
===Etymology===
{{dercat|de|gem-pro|inh=1}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|trinken}}, from {{inh|de|goh|trinkan}} (attested since the 8th century), from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*drinkan}}.<ref>Pfeifer, Wolfgang. 1995, 2005. ''Etymologisches Wörterbuch des Deutschen.'' München: dtv. {{ISBN|3423325119}}.</ref>

Germanic cognates with identical meaning include {{cog|osx|drinkan}} (and {{cog|nds|drinken}}), {{cog|odt|drinkan}} (and {{cog|nl|drinken}}, {{cog|af|drink}}), {{cog|ang|drincan}} (and Modern {{cog|en|drink}}), {{cog|ofs|drinka}} (and {{cog|fy|drinke}}), {{cog|non|drekka}} (and {{cog|is|drekka}}, {{cog|fo|dr

de:gehen.raw:
===Etymology===
{{ety|de|:inh|gmh:gān|tree=1}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|gān}}, {{m|gmh|gēn}}, from {{inh|de|goh|gān}}, {{m|goh|gēn}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*gān}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*gāną}}, from {{der|de|ine-pro|*ǵʰeh₁-||to leave}}.

Cognate with {{cog|nl|gaan}}, {{cog|nds|gaan}}, {{m|nds|gahn}}, {{cog|en|go}}, Swedish and Danish {{m|sv|gå}}, {{cog|yi|גיין}}.

The form ''gēn'' instead of ''gān'' is of Bavarian origin, but many dialects of Central and Low German have ''-e-'' (from earlier ''-ei-'') or ''ei'' in the 2nd and 3rd person singular present, in keeping with the Proto-Germanic irregular

de:kommen.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|[[quëmen]], [[komen]], [[kumen]]}}, from {{inh|de|goh|quëman}} (rarer {{m|goh|cuman}}, {{m|goh|chuman}}), from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*kweman}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*kwemaną}}, from {{der|de|ine-pro|*gʷem-}}. Cognate with {{cog|nds|-}} {{m|nds-de|kamen}}, {{cog|nl|komen}}, {{cog|en|come}}, {{cog|da|komme}}.

de:sein.raw:
===Etymology 1===
{{inh+|de|gmh|sīn}}, from {{inh|de|goh|sīn||to be}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*sīn}}, an analogical infinitive formed within the suppletive paradigm of “to be” from forms ultimately derived from {{der|de|ine-pro|*h₁es-||to be, exist}}. 

It replaced the older infinitive {{m|goh|wesan}}, from {{m|gem-pro|*wesaną||to be, remain}}. The paradigm is additionally suppleted with forms from {{m|gem-pro|*beuną||to be, exist, become}}.

Cognate with {{cog|nl|zijn||to be}}, {{cog|nds|sien||to be}}.

de:mögen.raw:
===Etymology===
{{ety|de|:inh|gmh:mugen}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|mugen}}, from {{inh|de|goh|mugan}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*magan}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*maganą}}, from {{der|de|ine-pro|*megʰ-}}. 

Compare {{cog|nl|mogen}}, {{cog|en|may}}, {{cog|is|mega}}, {{cog|got|𐌼𐌰𐌲𐌰𐌽}}, {{cog|sh|moći}}, {{cog|bg|мога}}.

The modern sense of "like" developed out of a negated "nicht mögen", shifting from "to not be able to do" to "to not like doing" in the 16th century<ref>{{R:de:Pfeifer}}</ref>, with the original sense "be able to" falling out of use in the 17th century.

See {{m|de|können}} for the orig

de:Morgen.raw:
===Etymology 1===
{{ety|de|id=morning|:inh|gmh:morgen<ety:inh<goh:morgan>>}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|morgen}}, from {{inh|de|goh|morgan}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*morgin|*morgan}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*murginaz|*murganaz}}, from {{der|de|ine-pro|*merkʷ-||to blink, twinkle}}. 

Compare {{cog|nds|Morgen}}, {{cog|nl|morgen}}, {{cog|fy|moarn}}, {{cog|en|morn}}, {{m|en|morrow}}, {{cog|da|morgen}}, {{cog|sv|morgon}}.

de:Abend.raw:
===Etymology===
{{ety|de|:inh|gmh:ābent<ety:inh<goh:āband>>}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|ābent}}, from {{inh|de|goh|āband}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*ābanþ}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*ēbanþs}}.

Compare {{cog|nds|Avend}}, {{cog|nl|avond}}, {{cog|en|even}} ({{m|en|evening}}), {{cog|non|aptann}}, {{cog|sv|afton}}, {{cog|no|-}} and {{cog|da|aften}}. Compare {{cog|en|eve}}.

de:heute.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|hiute}}, from {{inh|de|goh|hiutu}}, a contraction of earlier *{{m|goh|[[hēr|hiu]] [[tag|tagu]]}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*hiu dagu}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*hinō dagō|pos=from {{m|gem-pro|*hiz}} + {{m|gem-pro|*dagaz}}|t=on this day}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|hēodæġ|t=today}} and {{cog|nl|heden|t=today}}.
Compare {{cog|de|heuer}} from {{af|goh|hia|alt1=hiu|t1=in this|jār|alt2=jāru|t2=year|nocat=1}}.

de:hier.raw:
===Etymology===
{{dercat|de|gem-pro|inh=1}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|hier}}, from {{inh|de|goh|hier}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*hēr}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|hier}}, {{cog|en|here}}, {{cog|sv|här}}.

The predominant form in Middle High German and throughout modern dialects of [[High German]] is {{m|gmh|hie}} (and variants) with loss of the final ''-r''. The form {{m|de||hier}} began to gain ground from the late 16th century (in spite of Luther’s usage), which may point to influence by cognate {{der|de|gml|hīr}}, {{m|gml|hēr}} (where no ''r-''less form seems to exist; but compare modern {{cog|li|heej}}).

de:jetzt.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|iez}}, {{m|gmh|ieze}}, {{m|gmh|iezū}}, {{m|gmh|iezō}}, {{m|gmh|iezuo}}, from {{inh|de|goh|iozuo|t=straightaway, at once; further}}, equivalent to {{compound|de|je|zu|nocat=1}}. Compare {{cog|en|yet}}, {{cog|yi|יעצט}}.

de:klein.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|de|gmh|[[klein]], [[kleine]]}}, from {{inh|de|goh|kleini}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*klainī|t=shining, fine, splendid, tender}}, perhaps from {{der|de|ine-pro|*gleh₁y-|t=to cleave, stick}}. 

Cognate with {{cog|nl|klein}} and {{cog|en|clean}}. {{doublet|de|clean}}. For a similar semantic development, cf. ''[[zierlich]]'' (orig. "decorative", today "petite").

de:neu.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|niuwe}}, from {{inh|de|goh|niuwi}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*niwi}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*niwjaz}}, from {{inh|de|ine-pro|*néwos}}. 

Compare {{cog|nl|nieuw}}, {{cog|en|new}}, {{cog|da|ny}}, {{cog|got|𐌽𐌹𐌿𐌾𐌹𐍃}}.

de:Woche.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|woche}}, from {{inh|de|goh|wohha}}, alteration of older {{m|goh|wëhha}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*wikā}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*wikǭ}}, from {{der|de|ine-pro|*weyg-|t=to bend, wind, turn, yield}}. Compare {{cog|yi|וואָך}}, {{cog|en|week}}, {{cog|nl|week}}, {{cog|fy|wike}}, {{cog|da|uge}}, {{cog|sv|vecka}}.

de:spät.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|spǣte}}, from {{inh|de|goh|spāti}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*spādī}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*spēdiz}}. Cognate with {{cog|hrx|sped}}, from {{cog|nds|späd}}, archaic {{cog|nl|spade||late}}. Probably related to {{m|de|sparen||to spare, conserve}}.

de:immer.raw:
===Etymology===
{{ety|de|:inh|gmh:iemer|tree=1}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|iemer}} (also {{m|gmh|imer}}, {{m|gmh|immer}}), from {{der|de|goh|iomer|iomēr|always}}.

Cognate with {{cog|nl|immer}}, {{cog|gsw|immer}}, {{cog|nds-de|immer}}, {{m|nds-de|ümmer}}, {{m|nds-de|jümmer}}, {{m|nds-de|jümmers}}, {{cog|enm|a mare}}, {{m|enm|aa mare|t=evermore}}.

de:oft.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|ofte}}, {{m|gmh|oft}}, {{m|gmh|uft}}, from {{inh|de|goh|ofta}}, {{m|goh|ofto}}, {{m|goh|oftu}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*ufta}}, {{m|gem-pro|*uftō||often}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|oft}}, {{cog|en|oft}} and {{m|en|often}}.

de:Regen.raw:
===Etymology 1===
From {{inh|de|gmh|rëgen}}, from {{inh|de|goh|rëgan}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*regn}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*regną}}. Cognate with {{cog|yi|רעגן}}, {{cog|nl|regen}}, {{cog|en|rain}}, {{cog|da|regn}}.

de:Sonne.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|sunne}}, from {{inh|de|goh|sunna}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*sunnā}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*sunnǭ}}, from {{inh|de|ine-pro||*sh̥₂uén-}}, oblique stem of {{m|ine-pro|*sóh₂wl̥}}.

Akin to {{cog|nds|Sünn}}, {{m|nds|Zunne}}, {{cog|nl|zon}}, {{cog|en|sun}}, {{cog|fy|sinne}}, {{cog|is|sunna}}. Further Indo-European cognates include {{cog|la|sōl}}, {{cog|grc|ἥλιος}}, {{cog|sa|सूर्य||tr=sū́rya}}, {{cog|ru|солнце}}, {{cog|lt|saulė}}, {{cog|cy|haul}}.

de:Wolke.raw:
===Etymology===
{{dercat|de|gem-pro|ine-pro|inh=1}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|wolken}}, from {{inh|de|goh|wolkan}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*wolkn}}.

Akin to {{cog|nl|wolk}}, {{cog|en|welkin}}, {{cog|sla-pro|*volga}}, {{cog|sq|ulmej||to wet, dampen}}.

de:Gewitter.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{der|de|gmh|gewiter}}, {{m|gmh|gewitere}}, from {{inh|de|goh|giwitiri}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*gawidri}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*gawidriją}}, documented since the 9th century AD,<ref>{{cite-book|de|year=2005|author=Hermann Bluhme|title=Etymologisches Wörterbuch des deutschen Grundwortschatzes|page=356|isbn=3895868051}}</ref> equivalent to {{af|de|ge-|Wetter}}. Cognate with {{cog|hrx|Gewitter}}. Distantly cognate in structure to {{cog|en|aweather}}.

de:Nebel.raw:
===Etymology 1===
From {{inh|de|gmh|nëbel}}, from {{inh|de|goh|nëbul}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*nebulaz}}, from {{der|de|ine-pro|*nébʰos}} (whence also {{cog|ine-bsl-pro|*nébas}}, {{cog|iir-pro|*nábʰas}}, {{cog|grc|νεφέλη||cloud, mist}}, {{cog|la|nebula||mist, fog}}). More at {{cog|en|nuel}}.

de:Geld.raw:
===Etymology===
{{ety|de|:inh|gmh:gëlt<ety:inh<goh:gëlt<ety:inh<gmw-pro:*geld>>>>}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|gëlt}}, from {{inh|de|goh|gëlt}}, {{m|goh|këlt}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*geld}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*geldą||reward, gift, money}}, from {{der|de|ine-pro|*gʰeldʰ-||to pay}}. 

The modern consonantism ''-d'' instead of expected ''-t'' is [[Central German|Central]] and [[Low German]] (compare {{cog|gml|gelt}}, ''-des'', from {{cog|osx|geld}}); but also [[Upper German]] in some dialects through revoicing after ''-l-''. Compare {{cog|nl|geld}}, {{cog|en|geld}}, {{m|en|yield}}, {{cog|sv|gäld}}.

de:verkaufen.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|verkoufen}}, from {{inh|de|goh|firkoufen}}. Equivalent to {{prefix|de|ver|kaufen}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|verkopen}} and {{cog|yi|פֿאַרקויפֿן}}.

de:teuer.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|tiure}}, from {{inh|de|goh|tiuri}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*diurī}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*diurijaz}}, akin to {{cog|osx|diuri}}, compare {{cog|nl|duur}}, {{cog|en|dear}}, {{cog|is|dýr}}, and {{cog|sv|dyr}}.

de:traurig.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|trūrec}}, from {{inh|de|goh|trūrag}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*dreuzagaz|t=bloody}}, from {{der|de|ine-pro|*dʰreus-|t=to break, break off, crumble}}. {{surf|de|Trauer|-ig}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|treurig|t=sad, gloomy}}, {{cog|nds|trurig|t=sad}}, {{cog|hrx|traurich|t=sad}}, {{cog|en|dreary|t=grievous, dire, appalling, drab, dark, colourless, cheerless}}, {{cog|non|dreyrigr|t=bloody}}.

de:krank.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|krank}}, from {{inh|de|goh|*krank}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*krank}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*krangaz}}, {{m|gem-pro|*krankaz||crooked, weak}}. Cognate with {{cog|en|crank}}.

de:stolz.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|stolz}}, from {{inh|de|goh|stolz}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*stultaz||proud, stately, stiff}}, from {{der|de|ine-pro|*stel-||to put, stand}}; cognate with {{cog|en|stout}}.

de:zufrieden.raw:
===Etymology===
Since ca. 1500, from {{univerbation|de|zu|Frieden|nocap=1|lit=at peace}}. Likely a {{cal|de|gml|[[to|tô]] [[vrede|vrēde(n)]]|nocap=1}}, {{cal|de|dum|[[te]] [[vrēden]]|notext=1}} (modern {{m+|nl|tevreden}}), both of which date from the 13th century. Apart from the dating, this is also confirmed by the fact that the earliest High German attestations are from [[Hesse]] and the [[Rhineland]].

de:Gehalt.raw:
===Etymology 1===
From {{inh|de|gmh|gehalt}}, deverbal from {{m|gmh|gehalten|t=to keep still, retain, preserve, imprison}}, itself from {{m|gmh|halten|t=to hold}}. The earliest attested sense of the noun is “custody, prison”. In some southern dialects it also means “room, container, closet”. The modern sense develops in the 15th century, at first in the context of coins and metal alloys.

de:Zug.raw:
===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|de|id=procession|:inh|gmh:zuc<id:pull><ety:inh<goh:zug<id:pull><ety:inh<gmw-pro:*tugi<id:pull>>>>>}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|zuc}}, {{m|gmh|zug}}, from {{inh|de|goh|zug}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*tugi}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*tugiz}}, an abstract noun belonging to Proto-Germanic {{m|gem-pro|*teuhaną}}, from {{der|de|ine-pro|*dewk-||to pull, lead}}.<ref>{{R:EWddS|hw=Zug|ed=22}}</ref>

Cognate with {{cog|nl|teug}}, {{cog|nds|Tog}}, {{cog|hrx|Zugh}}, {{cognate|en|tug}}, {{cog|ang|tyġe}}. Related to and synchronically serving as the associated noun of {{m|de|ziehen||to pull, t

de:ankommen.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|anekomen}}, from {{inh|de|goh|anaqueman}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*anakweman}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*anakwemaną|t=to come to, come at, arrive}}. Compare {{cog|nl|aankomen}}, {{cog|en|oncome}}, {{cog|got|𐌰𐌽𐌰𐌵𐌹𐌼𐌰𐌽||}}.

de:links.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|linkes}}, originally the genitive of {{m|gmh|linc}}, whence modern {{m|de|link}}; see there for more. Cognate with {{cog|nl|links}}. {{surf|de|link|-s|id2=adverb}}.

de:Küche.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|küche}}, from {{inh|de|goh|chuhhina}}, from late {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*kukinā}}, from {{der|de|la-lat|cocīna}}, from earlier {{m|la|coquīna}}.

de:Garten.raw:
===Etymology===
{{root|de|ine-pro|*gʰerdʰ-}} {{dercat|de|gem-pro|ine-pro|inh=2}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|garte}}, from {{inh|de|goh|garto}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*gardō}}.

Cognate with {{cog|nl|gaarde}}, {{cog|en|yard}}, and through a Romance borrowing from Frankish: {{cog|en|garden}}, {{cog|fr|jardin}}, {{cog|es|jardín}}, {{cog|it|giardino}}. Also, cognate with Proto-Slavic {{m|sla-pro|*gȏrdъ}}, shifted to Russian {{m|ru|город}}, Polish {{m|pl|gród}} or Czech {{m|cs|hrad}}.

de:warten.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|warten}}, from {{inh|de|goh|wartēn}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*wardēn}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*wardāną}}. Cognate with {{cog|osx|wardōn}}, {{cog|sv|vårda}}, {{cog|en|ward}}.

de:verstehen.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|verstān}}, {{m|gmh|virstēn}}, {{m|gmh|vorstēn}}, {{m|gmh|ferstān}}, from {{inh|de|goh|firstān}}, {{m|goh|firstēn}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*frastāną}}, equivalent to {{prefix|de|ver|stehen}}. [[cognate|Cognate]] with {{cog|bar|versteh}}, {{cog|nl|verstaan}}, {{cog|gml|vorstān}}. Compare also {{cog|en|forstand}}.

de:können.raw:
===Etymology===
{{root|de|ine-pro|*ǵneh₃-}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|künnen}}, {{m|gmh|kunnen}}, from {{inh|de|goh|kunnan}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*kunnan}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*kunnaną}}, from {{der|de|ine-pro|*ǵneh₃-|t=to know}}.

The {{glossary|umlaut}}ed ''ö'' in the infinitive and plural present—as well as the umlaut in the other modal verbs {{m|de|mögen|t=to like}}, {{m|de|müssen|t=to have to}}{{,}} and {{m|de|dürfen|t=to be allowed to}}{{ref|group=n|name=n1|In Early New High German the modal verbs {{m|de|wollen|t=to want to}} and {{m|de|sollen|t=should}} also had umlauted variants {{m|de|wö

de:müssen.raw:
===Etymology===
{{dercat|de|gem-pro|inh=1}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|müeȥen}}, from {{inh|de|goh|muoȥan}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*mōtan}}.

The preservation of the original diphthong can still be seen in {{cog|bar|muass}}, the first and third person singular present form of {{m|bar|miassn}}.

See {{m|de|können}} for the origin of the historically unexpected {{glossary|umlaut}}.

de:denken.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|denken}}, from {{inh|de|goh|denken}}, {{m|goh|thenken}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*þankijan}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*þankijaną}}, from {{der|de|ine-pro|*teng-}}. 

Cognate with {{cog|bar|denkn}}, {{m|bar|denka}}, {{cog|nl|denken}}, {{m|nl|dinken}}, {{cog|nds|denken}}, {{m|nds|dinken}}, {{cog|fy|tinke}}, {{cog|en|think}}, {{cog|is|þekkja}}, {{cog|yi|דענקען}}.

de:wissen.raw:
===Etymology===
{{root|de|ine-pro|*weyd-}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|wiȥȥen}} and {{inh|de|goh|wiȥȥan}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*witan}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*witaną}}, from {{der|de|ine-pro|*wóyde|t=to see, to know}}.

Compare {{cog|nl|weten}}, {{cog|da|vide}}, {{cog|sv|veta}}, {{cog|en|wit}} and {{cog|la|videō|t=to see}}.

de:vielleicht.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|vil līchte||very easily}}, thus: “what could easily happen”. Compare the same in {{cog|nds-de|villicht}}, {{cog|nl|wellicht}}, {{cog|stq|fielicht}}.

de:genug.raw:
===Etymology===
{{root|de|ine-pro|*h₂neḱ-}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|genuoc}}, from {{inh|de|goh|ginuog}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*ganōg}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*ganōgaz}}.<ref>{{R:gem:PIEPG}}</ref>

Cognate with {{cog|nl|genoeg}}, {{cog|nds|(ge)noog}}, {{cog|en|enough}}, {{cog|fy|genôch}}, {{cog|da|nok}}, {{cog|sv|nog}}. ''Further Indo-European cognates:'' {{cog|la|nancīscor||to get, to obtain}}, {{cog|sl|nesti||to carry}}, {{cog|sq|kënaq||to satisfy}}.

de:zu.raw:
===Etymology===
From a spelling merger of two interrelated [[adprep]]s: 1.) {{inh|de|gmh|ze}}, from {{inh|de|goh|za}}, {{m|goh|zi}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*ta}}; and 2.) {{inh|de|gmh|zuo}}, from {{inh|de|goh|zuo}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*tō}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*tō}}. 

A distinction between both words has widely been retained in dialects, and also to some degree in modern spoken German (see pronunciation section below). Cognate with {{cog|sli|zu}} (contractions with the definite article: {{m|gmw-ecg|zum|g=m|g2=n}}, {{m|gmw-ecg|zur|g=f}}); {{cog|nl|te}}, {{m|nl|toe}}; {{cog|osx|tō}}; {{cog

de:noch.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|noch}}, {{m|gmh|nog}}, from {{inh|de|goh|noh}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*noh}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*nuh}}, from {{der|de|ine-pro|*nu||now}} + {{m|ine-pro|*-kʷe||and, also}}. Cognate to {{cog|nl|nog}} and {{m|nl|noch}} (which are etymologically the same word).

de:schon.raw:
===Etymology 1===
From {{inh|de|gmh|schōne|t=beautifully; appropriately; completely}}, from {{inh|de|goh|scōno|t=beautifully}}, adverb of {{m|goh|scōni}}, whence {{cog|de|schön|t=beautiful}}.<ref>[[w:Friedrich Kluge|Kluge, Friedrich]] (1975). ''Etymologisches Wörterbuch der deutschen Sprache''. 21st edition. Berlin: Walter de Gruyter. p. 675.</ref> For sense development from "''beautiful''" to "''indeed, surely; already''" compare {{m+|en|pretty}}.

de:auch.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|ouch}}, from {{inh|de|goh|ouh}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*auk}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|ook||also}}, {{cog|nds|ook||also}}, {{cog|fy|ek||also, too}}, {{cog|lb|och||also}}, {{cog|sv|och||and}}, {{cog|is|og||and}}, {{cog|da|og||and}}, and archaic {{cog|en|eke||also}}.

de:eher.raw:
===Etymology===
Chiefly from [[haplology]] of {{inh|de|gmh|ērer}}, from {{inh|de|goh|ēriro}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*airizô}}. Compare {{cog|nl|eerder}}.

Likely conflated with {{m+|gmh|ēr}}, a rarer byform of {{m|gmh|ē}} (whence modern {{m|de|[[eh]], [[ehe]]}}), from {{m+|goh|ēr}}, from {{m+|gem-pro|*airiz}}, adverbial form of the above. Cognate with {{cog|nl|eer}}, {{cog|en|ere}}, {{cog|got|𐌰𐌹𐍂𐌹𐍃}}. The final {{IPAchar|/r/}} was regularly lost in Late {{m+|goh|-}} (cf. {{m|de|[[da]], [[hie]], [[wo]]}}), but survived regionally (chiefly in [[Central German]]).

de:schnell.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|snël}}, from {{inh|de|goh|snël||nimble, brave, quick, lively}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*snel}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*snellaz||active, bold, quick}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|snel}}, {{cog|nds|snell}}, {{cog|en|snell}}. More at {{l|en|snell}}.

de:nur.raw:
===Etymology===
From late {{inh|de|gmh|nuor}}, contracted from older {{m|gmh|niwer}}, {{m|gmh|newære}}, from {{inh|de|goh|niwāri}}, {{m|goh|[[ni]] [[wāri]]||were it not}}. Cognate with {{cog|yi|נאָר}}, {{cog|nl|maar}}, {{cog|ang|nǣre}}.

de:Gesellschaft.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|gesellescaft}}, from {{inh|de|goh|giselliscaft}}. Equivalent to {{suffix|de|Geselle|schaft}}.

Cognate with {{cog|nl|gezelschap}}.

de:Umwelt.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{prefix|de|um|Welt}}. In the biological sense first used by {{w|Jakob Johann von Uexküll}} (1909).

de:Krankheit.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|krancheit}}, {{m|gmh|krankeit}}. {{surface analysis|de|krank|-heit}}; compare {{cog|gsw|Chranket}}, {{cog|lb|Krankheet}}. 

Eclipsed non-native {{ncog|gmh|malāze|t=sickness, disease}}, ultimately from Latin.

de:Lösung.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|lœsunge}}, {{m|gmh|lōsunge}}, from {{inh|de|goh|lōsunga|t=redemption, payment, ransom, fraud, deception}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*lausungu}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*lausungō}}, equivalent to {{suf|de|lösen|ung}}. Cognate with {{cog|en|leasing}}, {{cog|gsw|Lösig}}, {{cog|is|lausung}}. Compare also {{cog|nl|oplossing}}.

de:Grund.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|grunt}}, from {{inh|de|goh|grunt}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*grundu}}, from {{der|de|gem-pro|*grunduz}}, from {{der|de|ine-pro|*gʰr̥mtu-}}. 

Cognate with {{cog|fy|grûn}}, {{cog|nl|grond}}, {{cog|en|ground}}. Non-Germanic cognates include {{cog|sq|grundë||brittle earth}} and {{m|sq|gryej||to erode, crumble}}.<ref name="DWDS Etym">[http://www.dwds.de/?qu=Grund&source=osplugin DWDS (Digitales Wörterbuch der deutschen Sprache): '''Grund'''].</ref>

de:Ziel.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|zil}}, from {{inh|de|goh|zil}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*til}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*tilą}}. Cognate to {{cog|ang|til}}.

de:scheitern.raw:
===Etymology===
Verbal formation from {{inh|de|gmh|schīt}},<ref>{{R:Kluge 1891|scheitern}}</ref> synchronically analyzed as {{af|de|Scheiter|-n|t1=plural of {{m|de|Scheit|t=log, stick of firewood}}|t2=verbal suffix}}. The modern sense of "to fail" is derived from figurative usage of the verb as "to fall to pieces (logs)" > "to fail" (DWDS).

de:wählen.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|weln}}, from {{m|gmh|welen}}, {{m|gmh|wellen}}, from {{inh|de|goh|wellen}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*walljan}}, from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*waljaną}}, ultimately from {{der|de|ine-pro|*welh₁-}}.

de:ändern.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|endern}}, more at {{m|de|anderer||other, different}}. Cognate with {{cog|hrx|ennre}}.

de:schwierig.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|swiric}}, {{m|gmh|sweric||full of boils}}, a derivative of {{m|de|Schwäre|t=ulcer}}. Cognate to dated {{cog|nl|zwerig||full of boils}}. Often connected to its synonym {{m|de|schwer}}, but unrelated.

de:notwendig.raw:
===Etymology===
An early modern German formation: {{compound|de|Not|t1=need|wendig|t2=maneuverable, agile}}, originally “necessary to avert the distress”, compare ''die Not'' {{m|de|abwenden}}.

de:klar.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{der|de|gmh|klār}}, {{m|gmh|clār}}, formally from {{der|de|gml|klār}} or {{der|de|dum|claer}} and reinforced by {{der|de|fro|cler}}, both from {{der|de|la|clārus|t=bright}}.<ref>{{R:EWddS|ed=22|hw=klar}}</ref> {{doublet|de|klaro}}.

de:deshalb.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|deshalp}}, from {{der|de|gmh|des}}, {{m|gmh|dez|t=from that, therefore, thereon}} + {{m|gmh|halp|t=half}}. Cognate to {{cog|nds|diäßhalw}} {{q|Paderbornisch}}.

de:obwohl.raw:
===Etymology===
{{univerbation|de|ob|wohl}}, from the older use of {{m|de|ob}} as a conditional and concessive conjunction, reinforced with an adverb. Compare {{m|de|obgleich}}, {{m|de|obschon}}, {{m|de|obzwar}} and also {{m|de|gleichwohl}}.

de:trotz.raw:
===Etymology===
{{ellipsis|de|[[zum]] [[Trotz]] ([[dem]])}} or from constructions with the dative verb {{m|de|trotzen}}. Compare {{m|de|trotzdem}}.

de:ungefähr.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|ân gevœre}}, mostly {{inh|de|gmh|ân gevœrde||without evil intention, without deceit}}.  Equivalent to {{m|de|ohne||without}} + {{m|de|Gefahr||threat, danger, peril}}.<ref>{{R:Kluge 1891|ohngefähr}}</ref> Cognate with {{cog|nl|ongeveer}}.

de:wegen.raw:
===Etymology===
Shortened version of {{m|de||von + [genitive object] + wegen}}, from {{inh|de|gmh|[[von]] + [genitive object] + [[wegen]]}}, with {{m|gmh|wegen}} being the dative plural of {{m|gmh|wec}}, modern-day {{m|de|Weg}}, but with a meaning similar to {{m|de|[[Ort]], [[Stelle]], [[Seite]]}}.

de:Vorteil.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|vorteil}}, {{m|gmh|voreteil}}, from {{inh|de|goh|forateila}}, equivalent to {{prefix|de|vor|t1=before, better|Teil|t2=part, piece}}. Compare {{cog|en|foredeal|t=advantage, benefit}}.

de:Unterschied.raw:
===Etymology===
From the fusion of {{inh|de|gmh|underschiet}}, {{m|gmh|underschit}}, {{inh|de|gmh|underschide}}, and {{inh|de|gmh|underscheit}}, {{m|gmh|unterscheid}}, from {{inh|de|goh|untarskeit}}, {{m|goh|untarskeid}}; derived synchronically from {{m|de|unterscheiden}}. Compare {{cog|nl|onderscheid}}, {{cog|hrx|Unnerschied}}, {{cog|nds|Ünnerscheed}}, {{cog|stq|Unnerskeed}}.

de:Tendenz.raw:
===Etymology===
Relatinized from {{der|de|fr|tendance}} under the influence of {{der|de|la-med|tendentia}}.

de:fördern.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|vürdern}}, from {{inh|de|goh|furdiren}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*furþrijan}}. Equivalent to archaic {{affix|de|fürder|t1=further|-n}}. The modern ⟨ö⟩ corresponds to the variant {{m|de||förder}}, which probably developed through conflation with related {{m|de|vorder}} (whence {{m|de|fordern}}), but may have been reinforced by regular {{der|de|gml|[[vȫrder]], [[vȫrderen]]}}. Cognate with {{m+|en|further}}, which see.

de:allerdings.raw:
===Etymology===
Compound of {{af|de|aller|pos1=genitive plural of {{m|de|alle||all}}|Dings|pos2=genitive singular of {{m|de|Ding||thing}}}} (compare {{m|de|schlechterdings}}). Before the 19th century, the full form {{m|de|aller [[Dinge]]||of all things}}, with the plural {{m|de|Dinge}}, was used.

de:Wachstum.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|wahstuom}}, ultimately from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*wahstmaz||growth}}. {{surf|de|wachsen|-tum}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|wæstm|t=growth, increase, produce, fruit}}.

fr:problématique.e: central research question, framing of a problem
fr:problématique.raw:
===Etymology===
{{lbor|fr|la-lat|problēmaticus}}, itself borrowed from {{der|fr|grc|προβληματικός}}, from {{m|grc|πρόβλημα||outjutting, barrier, problem}} (whence {{m|fr|problème}}).

fr:échantillon.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{uder|fr|fro|eschandillon||standard}}, from {{uder|fr|fro|eschandiller||to verify the measures of merchants}}, — a primarily Lyonnais word, from {{uder|fr|la|scandaculum||ladder}}, from {{uder|fr|la|scandere||to climb}}.

fr:dépouillement.e: processing/analysis of data; counting of votes / vote count

fr:portée.raw:
===Etymology===
From feminine past participle of {{m|fr|porter||to carry}}.

fr:acception.e: sense, accepted meaning of a word

fr:amorce.raw:
===Etymology===
Corruption of {{inh|fr|fro|amorse}}, form of {{m|fro|amordre}}, a compound of {{m|fro|mordre}}.

fr:jalon.raw:
===Etymology===
1613, ''jallon'', in an unknown sense; 1690 in gardening; uncertain origin, maybe from ''jalir'', ancient form of {{m|fr|jaillir||to spurt out}}.

fr:volet.e: strand, component, part of a plan

fr:inflexion.e: shift in direction, change of emphasis

fr:relever.e: to note, point out; to raise (a level)

fr:soutenir.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|soustenir}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|sustenir}}, {{m|fro|soustenir}}, from {{inh|fr|la-vul|*sustenīre}}, from {{inh|fr|la|sustineō|sustinēre}}. Asynchronically analyzable as {{af|fr|sou-|tenir}}.

fr:tempérer.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{der|fr|fro|temprer}}; the ''é'' was added to make it more closely match the {{bor|fr|la|-}} spelling {{m|la|tempero|temperō, temperāre}}. This form may also be seen as a learned borrowing from the Latin word (according to the TLFi), and used in the sense of "temper", "sooth" as opposed to the sense relating to soaking or drenching (cf. the popularly evolved form {{doublet|fr|tremper|notext=1}}).

fr:récuser.e: to reject, challenge, take exception to

fr:reposer sur.e: to rest on, be based on

fr:induire.raw:
===Etymology===
{{bor+|fr|la|indūcō|indūcere}} (or altered from the Old French form {{m|fr|enduire}}). Compare the inherited doublet {{doublet|fr|enduire|notext=1}}.

fr:supposer.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|frm|supposer}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|supposer}}, borrowed from {{bor|fr|la|suppōnō|suppōnere}}, altered based on French {{m|fr|poser}}.

fr:postuler.e: to postulate; to apply for a post

fr:cerner.e: to pin down, get to grips with

fr:recenser.e: to survey, list, take a census of

fr:dégager.e: to bring out, identify (a trend); to clear

fr:déceler.e: to detect, uncover / to detect / discern / glimpse

fr:discerner.raw:
===Etymology===
{{lbor|fr|la|discernō|discernere}}, assimilated into the first conjugation group (regular ''-er'' suffixed verbs).

fr:ébaucher.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{uder|fr|frm|esbaucher||to rough-hew, frame}}, alteration (due to {{cog|frm|bauche||beam, wooden crosspiece}}) of {{uder|fr|fro|esbosquier}}, {{m|fro|esboskier||to rough-hew beams}}, from {{m|fro|es-||out}} + {{m|fro|bosc||wood, firewood}}, from {{der|fr|frk|*bosk||wood}}, from {{uder|fr|gem-pro|*buskaz||wood, thicket}}. Cognate with {{cog|fro|esbochier||to prune grapes}}, {{cog|fr|bois||wood}}, {{m|fr|bau||beam}}. More at {{m|en|bush}}, {{m|en|balk}}.

fr:élaborer.e: to develop, work out in detail

fr:décliner.e: to break down into variants; to decline (an offer)

fr:s'inscrire dans.e: to fit within, form part of

fr:relever de.e: to fall under, be a matter for

fr:tenir à.e: to be due to, stem from; to be attached to

fr:témoigner de.e: to attest to, bear witness to

fr:rendre compte de.e: to account for, give an account of

fr:faire état de.e: to report, make mention of / to report, cite

fr:s'avérer.e: to prove to be, turn out to be

fr:recouvrir.e: to cover, encompass (a range of meanings)

fr:infondé.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{af|fr|in-|fondé}}, attested since the nineteenth century.

fr:exhaustif.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{der|fr|la|exhaustus}}, past participle of {{m|la|exhaurio|exhaurīre|to draw out, drink up, empty, exhaust}}, + {{af|fr|-if}}.

fr:ambivalent.raw:
===Etymology===
{{bor+|fr|de|ambivalent}}, from {{af|fr|la:ambi-|la:valēns}}, the latter from the verb {{m|la|valeō}}.

fr:sujet à caution.e: questionable, to be treated with caution

fr:afférent.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{der|fr|la|afferēns}}. Compare the now obsolete verb {{m|fr|afférir}}.

fr:empirique.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{der|fr|frm|empirique}}, from {{der|fr|fro|empirique}}, borrowed from {{der|fr|la|empīricus}}, itself a borrowing from {{der|fr|grc|ἐμπειρικός}}.

Cognate with {{cog|en|empiric}} via Old French.

fr:révélateur.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{af|fr|révéler|-ateur}}. The adjectival sense is the attributive form of the noun.

fr:obsolète.raw:
===Etymology===
Partly from {{inh|fr|frm|obsolet}}, partly directly {{bor+|fr|la|obsolētus|t=worn out, gone out of use|nocap=1}}.<ref>{{R:FEW|7|286|obsoletus}}</ref>

fr:or.raw:
===Etymology 1===
From {{inh|fr|frm|or}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|or}}, from {{inh|fr|la|aurum}}, from {{inh|fr|itc-pro|*auzom}}, from {{der|fr|ine-pro|*h₂é-h₂us-o-||glow}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*h₂ews-||to dawn, become light, become red}}.

fr:reste.raw:
===Etymology 1===
{{inh+|fr|frm|reste}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|reste}}, equivalent to the stem of {{m|fr|rester}}.

fr:en l'occurrence.e: in this instance, as it happens

fr:cas échéant.e: where applicable, if need be / should the case arise

fr:sorte.raw:
===Etymology===
{{inh+|fr|fro|sorte}}, borrowed from {{bor|fr|la|sors|sortem}}. Doublet of the inherited {{doublet|fr|sort|notext=1}}.

fr:en tout état de cause.raw:
===Etymology===
{{lit|in all state of case|whatever the advancement of the case may be}}, from {{m|fr|cause}} in the sense of "(legal) case".

fr:il n'en demeure pas moins que.t: il n'en demeure pas moins que

fr:nonobstant.raw:
===Etymology===
{{univerbation|fr|non|obstant}}, Old French participle of {{m|fro|obster||to obstruct, stand in the way of}}, from {{inh|fr|fro|non obstant}}.
Akin to {{cog|it|nonostante}}, {{cog|es|no obstante}} and {{cog|pt|não obstante}}.

Compare also {{noncog|nl|niettegenstaande}} and {{noncog|en|notwithstanding}} for a similar construction.

fr:au regard de.e: with regard to, in light of

fr:compte tenu de.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{m|fr|tenir compte}}, converted into a [[nominative absolute]].

fr:à l'aune de.e: measured against, by the yardstick of
fr:à l'aune de.raw:
===Etymology===
{{lit|by the [[ell]] of}}, the ell being a unit of measure (often for cloth).

fr:s'agissant de.e: as regards, when it comes to

fr:quant à.raw:
===Etymology===
Compare {{cog|pt|quanto a}}, {{cog|it|quanto a|(in) quanto a}}, {{cog|ast,es|en cuanto a}}.

fr:faute de.e: for want of, in the absence of

fr:à défaut de.e: failing that, in the absence of

fr:il n'est pas exclu que.e: it cannot be ruled out that

fr:il est permis de penser que.t: il est permis de penser que

fr:on est en droit de se demander.t: on est en droit de se demander

fr:peu ou prou.e: more or less, to some degree

fr:tant bien que mal.e: after a fashion, somehow or other

fr:naguère.raw:
===Etymology===
From the French expression ''({{l|fr|il}}) {{l|fr|n'}}({{l|fr|y}}) {{l|fr|a}} {{l|fr|guère}} ({{l|fr|de}} {{l|fr|temps}})'' ("not long ago"), composed of ''{{l|fr|il y a}}'' (“ago”) + ''{{l|fr|guère|ne... guère}}'' (“hardly”).

fr:jadis.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{uder|fr|fro|ja a dis||there are days before}}, from {{m|fro|ja||already}} + {{m|fro|a||has}} + plural of {{m|fro|di||day}}.

fr:dorénavant.raw:
===Etymology===
{{univerbation|fr}} of {{der|fr|fro|[[d']][[ore]] [[en avant]]||from now forward}}.
Cognate with {{cog|pt|doravante}} and {{cog|it|d'ora in avanti}}.

fr:dresser un état des lieux.e: to take stock of the situation

fr:faire fi de.e: to disregard, snap one's fingers at

fr:pallier une carence.e: to make up for a shortcoming

fr:Il importe de préciser que.e: It is important to clarify that…

fr:Précisons d'emblée que.e: Let us clarify at the outset that…

fr:Cette étude s'inscrit dans le prolong.t: Cette étude s'inscrit dans le prolongement de

fr:À la suite des travaux de.t: À la suite des travaux de

fr:Contrairement à ce que l'on pourrait.t: Contrairement à ce que l'on pourrait croire
fr:Contrairement à ce que l'on pourrait.e: Contrary to what one might think…

fr:Il n'en va pas de même pour.t: Il n'en va pas de même pour
fr:Il n'en va pas de même pour.e: The same does not hold for…

fr:Reste à savoir si.e: It remains to be seen whether…

de:begründen.e: to justify, give reasons for; to found
de:begründen.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|begründen||to found, solidify}}. Equivalent to {{prefix|de|be|gründen|t2=to establish, build}}. The figurative meaning of [[reason]] comes from {{m|de|Grund}}.

de:belegen.e: to substantiate, provide evidence for; to occupy (a seat, a place)

de:beziffern.e: to put a figure on, quantify (at)

de:bewältigen.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{m|de|be-}} + {{suffix|de|waltig|en}}, in which ''waltig'' is an obsolete variant of {{m|de|gewaltig}}.<ref>{{R:de:Grimm|w=waltig}}</ref>

de:beeinträchtigen.raw:
===Etymology===
Not directly related to {{m|de|Eintracht|t=concord, harmony}}, but instead from another {{m|de||Eintracht}}, which was an [[East Central German]] variant of {{m|de|Eintrag|t=impairment}}. The earliest attestations of the verb are apparently from the 16th century. Regardless, both "Eintracht"s derive from the same root.

de:bekunden.raw:
===Etymology===
Borrowed from {{bor|de|nds-de|-}}, from {{m|de|be-}} + {{m|nds|kunden}}, Central German form of {{m|de|künden|t=to announce, tell}}.

de:beschwichtigen.raw:
===Etymology===
Via {{bor|de|nds-de|-}} from {{bor|de|gml|beswichtigen}}. Pertaining to {{cog|nl|zwichten}} and {{cog|goh|giswiftēn}} with the Low German (and Dutch) development ''-ft-'' → ''-cht-'' (compare {{m|de|Nichte}}). Ultimately related to {{der|de|gem-pro|*swībaną}}.

de:ergründen.e: to fathom, get to the bottom of

de:erübrigen.e: to spare (time, money); *(sich ~)* to be superfluous
de:erübrigen.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{affix|de|er-|übrig|t2=remaining, left over|-en}}, hence “to leave over, have as surplus”. Accordingly, the reflexive {{m|de||sich erübrigen}} actually means “to be left, remain” and one would originally say {{m|de||es erübrigt sich, etwas zu tun}} in the sense of “XY still remains to be done”. The quite opposite contemporary sense seems to emerge around 1900. It probably developed through confusion with the active verb in the sense of “to spare”. Moreover, that which is left to be done last is often the least important thing and may in fact become redundant through devel

de:obgleich.raw:
===Etymology===
{{univerbation|de|ob|gleich}}, from the older use of {{m|de|ob}} as a conditional and concessive conjunction, reinforced with an adverb. Compare {{m|de|obwohl}}, {{m|de|obschon}}, {{m|de|obzwar}} and also {{m|de|gleichwohl}}.

de:es sei denn.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{inh|de|gmh|ez ne sî denne}}<ref>§ 338 in Hermann Paul: Mittelhochdeutsche Grammatik<sup>19</sup>. Bearbeitet von F. Saran, E. Gierach, O. Behagel, L. E. Schmitt und Walther Mitzka. Tübingen: Max Niemeyer Verlag 1963.</ref>, a stereotypical ''negatively exceptive sentence''. The simple negation {{m|gmh|ne}} had been gradually vanishing since medieval times and had been dropped entirely by Luther's time. Since the disappearance of ''ne'', the negative function has been assumed by ''denn'' (or ''dann''), meaning "then" (i.e. "at that time"), which was originally facultative

de:angesichts.raw:

From the genitive case of {{m|de|Angesicht}}, preserving the original sense of "viewing, sight".

de:seitens.raw:
===Etymology===
From prepositional phrases with {{m|de|Seite}} with a calcified inflectional {{m|de|-en}} (compare e.g. {{m|de|aufseiten}}) with a secondary adverbial {{af|de|-s|id1=adverb}}.

de:binnen.raw:
===Etymology===
From {{der|de|gml|binnen||within}}, ultimately from {{inh|de|gem-pro|*bi-||by, at}} + {{m|gem-pro|*innan}} << {{m|gem-pro|*in||in}}. The form is also [[Central German]] in {{inh|de|gmh|binnen}} (compare {{cog|lb|bannen}}). It is originally an adverb meaning “within, inside” chiefly in local sense, equivalent to German {{m|de|innen}}. ''Binnen'' was adopted in modern standard German as a temporal preposition, while the prefix {{m|de|binnen-}} takes on the local sense of the word. Cognate with {{cog|nl|binnen}}.

de:jenseits.raw:
